title: Field Galois group and the finite etale geometric fibre functor
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $\Omega/K$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\widetilde\Omega/\Omega$ an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Give $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ the Krull topology: the subgroups fixing finite intermediate extensions pointwise form a neighbourhood basis of the identity. Put $s:\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $F_s$ be the finite etale fibre functor [def-galois-categories, def-galois-fibre-functor]. Every $\sigma\in G$ has a unique $K$-automorphism extension $\widetilde\sigma$ of $\widetilde\Omega$. The formula
$$j(\sigma)_Q(t)=t\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde\sigma)$$
for finite etale $K$-schemes $Q$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega\to Q$ defines an isomorphism of profinite topological groups
$$j:G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}K,s).$$
For $r:\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, precomposition gives a bijection, natural in finite etale $Q/K$,
$$b_Q:\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}|Q_s|,\qquad u\longmapsto u\circ r.$$
It satisfies $b_Q(u\circ\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)=j(\sigma)_Q(b_Q(u))$.

source.place: Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group (both parts and the displayed equality of Hom sets in the proof); Tag 0BQ9, remark-variance (extension to the algebraic closure and the explicit action).

proof.text: First extend automorphisms. For each $x\in\widetilde\Omega$, the simple extension $\Omega(x)/\Omega$ is finite (powers below the degree of an annihilating polynomial span it). Apply [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable] to this extension: its bottom field is separably closed by [def-pd-separable-closure]. Thus $\widetilde\Omega/\Omega$ is purely inseparable, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. In characteristic zero it equals $\Omega$; in characteristic $p>0$ each $x$ has a power $x^{p^n}\in\Omega$. Given $\sigma\in G$, view the same algebraically closed field $\widetilde\Omega$ with the two embeddings $i:\Omega\hookrightarrow\widetilde\Omega$ and $i\sigma$. Both are algebraic closures of $\Omega$ since their images coincide. The uniqueness-up-to-isomorphism clause of [def-weil-algebraic-closure] gives a field automorphism $\widetilde\sigma$ with $\widetilde\sigma i=i\sigma$. Two such extensions agree: their values on $x$ have the same $p^n$-th power $\sigma(x^{p^n})$, and Frobenius is injective in a field. The characteristic-zero case is immediate. Uniqueness also gives $\widetilde{\sigma\tau}=\widetilde\sigma\widetilde\tau$.

source.place: Tag 0BQ9, remark-variance, the algebraic closure is the perfection of the separable closure

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] with intermediate field $K$, $\Omega/K$ is normal and separable algebraic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to write $Q=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ with $L_i/K$ finite separable. The index set is finite: $Q/K$ is finite, hence its underlying affine algebra is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; the component idempotents are linearly independent in this finite-dimensional algebra, since restriction to any component sends its own idempotent to $1$ and every other one to $0$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a point in this component is an embedding $L_i\to\widetilde\Omega$. The minimal polynomial of every $a\in L_i$ splits in $\Omega$: it is separable, and $\Omega$ is separably closed. Consequently every possible image of $a$ in $\widetilde\Omega$ is in $\Omega$, by evaluating that product of linear factors in a field. Thus this embedding factors uniquely through $\Omega$. This proves that $b_Q$ is bijective, including $Q=\varnothing$. Postcomposition with any $K$-morphism $Q\to Q'$ commutes with precomposition by $r$, so the bijections are natural.

source.place: Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group, proof of part (1), equality of Hom sets

proof.text:
Contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde{\sigma\tau})=\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde\tau)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde\sigma)$. Hence $j(\sigma\tau)_Q(t)=j(\sigma)_Q(j(\tau)_Q(t))$. Identity and inverses follow likewise. Postcomposition with a map of finite etale schemes commutes with these operations, so this is a natural automorphism of $F_s$. The equality $\widetilde\sigma i=i\sigma$ gives $r\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde\sigma)=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ r$. Therefore
$$j(\sigma)_Q(b_Q(u))=u\circ r\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde\sigma)=u\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ r=b_Q(u\circ\operatorname{Spec}\sigma).$$

source.place: Tag 0BQ9, remark-variance, displayed action and multiplication calculation

proof.text: The restriction map of [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit], applicable because step 2 proves $\Omega/K$ Galois, identifies $G$ topologically with the compatible tuples in the product of the finite groups $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$. This is a closed subgroup: for every inclusion $L\subseteq M$, the equation $g_M|_L=g_L$ cuts out the inverse image of the diagonal in a finite discrete set; intersect these closed equations. Thus [lem-galois-closed-subgroup-product-finite-groups] makes $G$ profinite, in particular compact Hausdorff. Its identity has the required basis of open subgroups by the Krull topology in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0BNE part (2); field-theoretic input Stacks Tag 0BU2, fields-lemma-infinite-galois-limit

proof.text: Apply the compact alternative of [lem-sfb-complete-group-forgetful-automorphisms] to $G$, with the Hausdorff, compactness and open-subgroup-basis hypotheses checked in step 4. It identifies $G$ with the automorphism group of the underlying-set functor on its orbit category $\mathcal O_G$. Every orbit $G/U$ in this category is finite: the open cosets of $U$ cover compact $G$, and a finite subcover contains every distinct coset. Thus every object of $\mathcal O_G$ is a finite transitive continuous $G$-set.

source.place: Tag 0BNE part (2), reconstruction of the group from its action category; compact reconstruction supplied by Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 7.1.5 and Example 7.1.6

proof.text: Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_s)$. Transport it through $b$ to $a_Q=b_Q^{-1}\alpha_Qb_Q$ on $H(Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,Q)$. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification], for every orbit $O=G/U$ choose a finite separable field $L_O/K$ and an equivariant bijection $c_O:H(\operatorname{Spec}L_O)\to O$. These spectra are finite etale: finiteness is [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etaleness is [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. Set $a_O=c_Oa_{\operatorname{Spec}L_O}c_O^{-1}$. Every equivariant map $O\to O'$ is induced, through $c_O,c_{O'}$, by a unique $K$-morphism of the corresponding spectra, by the full-faithfulness clause of the classification. Naturality of $a_Q$ therefore proves naturality of $a_O$; applying the same construction to $\alpha^{-1}$ proves invertibility. Step 5 now gives a unique $\sigma\in G$ acting as $a_O$ on every orbit. The same full-faithfulness clause, applied to an equivariant isomorphism from $H(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ to a chosen orbit representative, implies $a_{\operatorname{Spec}L}(u)=u\circ\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$ for every finite separable $L/K$. For general $Q$, its decomposition in step 2 and naturality along each component inclusion give this equality on every point of $H(Q)$. Step 3 gives $\alpha=j(\sigma)$. Uniqueness from reconstruction also proves injectivity: if $j(\sigma)=j(\tau)$ their actions on all these orbit representatives coincide, so $\sigma=\tau$.

source.place: Tag 0BNE part (1) and part (2); Tag 03QR, lemma-sheaves-point, orbit classification and full faithfulness

proof.text: Check the topology explicitly, using [def-galois-aut-topology]. For $u\in H(Q)$ in the $L$-component, its stabilizer in $G$ fixes the finite subfield $u^\sharp(L)\subseteq\Omega$ pointwise and is open by the stated Krull basis. The kernel of the action on the finite set $H(Q)$ is the finite intersection of these open stabilizers. Thus every map $G\to\operatorname{Aut}(F_s(Q))$ is continuous, and so $j$ is continuous for the product-induced topology. Conversely, for any open subgroup $U\subseteq G$, choose the orbit $G/U$ and its finite separable field representative as in step 6. The identity coset corresponds to a point $x$ of its geometric fibre. Since its stabilizer is exactly $U$, the bijection $j$ sends $U$ onto the stabilizer of $x$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(F_s)$. This latter subgroup is open in the product-induced topology. Hence $j^{-1}$ is continuous at the identity (open subgroups form a basis), and by translation everywhere. Together with steps 3, 4 and 6 this makes $j$ an isomorphism of profinite topological groups.

source.place: Tag 0BNE part (2); Tag 0BQ9 explicit action; topology from section-galois, equation-embedding-product

proof.text: Finally the finite-etale fibre-functor interpretation of $\pi_1$ agrees with the finite-locally-constant-sheaf interpretation in [def-galois-fibre-functor]: [thm-galois-lc-etale] supplies an equivalence compatible with these fibre functors. Conjugation by that natural fibre isomorphism identifies their natural automorphisms; the inverse uses the inverse equivalence. Its coordinate maps are bijections of finite fibres, so it also identifies their product-induced topologies. Thus the group just identified is the stated $\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$, with exactly the action and natural equivariance formula proved in step 3.

source.place: Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group, fibre-functor compatibility; finite-etale/FLC identification in thm-galois-lc-etale

The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint block are identical to live. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so no other group has superseded it. There are no new nodes, no cycle, and proof_deps equal the union of the step uses. Step checks: (1) Omega(x)/Omega is finite, hence purely inseparable by the kun lemma. The two embeddings i and i·sigma make Omega~ an algebraic closure twice, so the uniqueness clause gives sigma~, and Frobenius injectivity makes it unique (K not assumed perfect). (2) cite (2) with k'=K makes Omega/K Galois. The etale-fibre lemma at the single point gives Q as a disjoint union of Spec L_i, finitely many by independence of the idempotents. Each embedding L_i into Omega~ lands in Omega because the separable polynomials split there. (3) Spec(sigma tau)=Spec tau∘Spec sigma, a left action as in 0BQ9; the identity r∘Spec sigma~ = Spec sigma∘r is checked. (4) Krull limit plus a closed subgroup of a product of finite groups gives G profinite. (5) Compact case of lem-sfb-complete-group-forgetful-automorphisms; the orbits G/U are finite. (6) The classification's converse and full-faithfulness clauses make the transported automorphism natural on the orbit category. This gives sigma, extended to every finite separable L via H(g)^{-1} sigma H(g) and then to every Q through its components; injectivity comes from reconstruction. (7) Stab(u) is the fixer of u#(L), so j is continuous. For open U, j(U)=Stab(x), so j is open and hence a homeomorphism. (8) The FEt/FLC equivalence compatible with fibre functors (thm-galois-lc-etale) transfers the group and its topology to pi_1 as defined in def-galois-fibre-functor. Edge cases checked: Q empty, K separably closed, characteristic 0, imperfect K, the trivial orbit.
